nodes.label: Can explain Ricart-Agrawala Algorithm
nodes.description: The Ricart-Agrawala Algorithm is a distributed mutual exclusion algorithm that uses Lamport timestamps to order requests for critical section access.

nodes.label: Can analyze bandwidth usage of Ricart-Agrawala
nodes.description: The Ricart-Agrawala Algorithm has a bandwidth usage of 2*(N-1) messages per enter operation, which can be high for large N.

nodes.label: Can explain Maekawa's Algorithm
nodes.description: Maekawa's Algorithm reduces the number of replies needed for mutual exclusion by using voting sets, allowing only a subset of processes to grant permission.

nodes.label: Can identify safety in Maekawa's Algorithm
nodes.description: Safety in Maekawa's Algorithm is ensured because a process can only receive replies from its voting set, preventing multiple processes from entering the critical section simultaneously.

nodes.label: Can analyze performance of Maekawa's Algorithm
nodes.description: Maekawa's Algorithm has improved bandwidth usage compared to Ricart-Agrawala, with O(√N) messages per enter operation, making it more efficient for large systems.

nodes.label: Can explain leader election in distributed systems
nodes.description: Leader election is a process in distributed systems to select a single process as the coordinator or leader among a group of processes.

nodes.label: Can describe the Ring Election Algorithm
nodes.description: The Ring Election Algorithm organizes processes in a logical ring and uses message passing to elect a leader based on attributes.

nodes.label: Can identify safety and liveness in election algorithms
nodes.description: Election algorithms must ensure safety by electing one leader and liveness by guaranteeing that the election process terminates successfully.
